item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: My favourite read of the History Contest so far. A strong, distinct character voice, a story that makes the most of limited perspective, and a neat take on a well-known anomaly. This is excellent, and deserving of the high praise it's getting. Strongly recommended to those who haven't read it yet.

item.content:encoded: This is legitimately my favorite piece of prose on the wiki. It's everything the Canon should be, and more. Goddamn, this is some fine stuff.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Flyboy prose and knife-edge tensions set amidst a solid intersection of the real and the supernatural that Coldest War material is known for. This is one kickass piece. +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Another reminder that 'adventure' means different things when you're living it.

The image of completely mundane humans flying a fragile construct twelve miles up at the risk of being exploded by an assault from the ground is almost as anomalous as the Foundation's contribution.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really enjoy the grounded (even though it's a plane hardeeharhar) feel of this one. It's also one of the best examples of the "shut up and don't ask questions" mindset that must be prevalent all throughout the Foundation's interactions with the world.
+1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Well that's a far out tale. The idea of using the U2 program to snap photos and then the Iris's of the world to reach into those photos for long range espionage is both hilarious and quite brilliant. On top of that, the story is nice in that its just the right length to leave an impact, but not so long as to drag on or overstay its welcome.

+1 vez. Nice job.
